problem: Service robots need scene understanding for autonomous navigation, but conventional geometric grid maps lack semantic information and depth-camera-only systems are hard to plug into laser-based 2D navigation stacks.
motivation: Scene understanding is a prerequisite of navigation and navigation is its goal, so a map that carries semantics lets service robots interact better with people and environments. Only the abstract is available, so details are limited.
key_idea: Build a dense point-cloud map with a deep CNN, convert depth-camera data into simulated laser data to build a 2D grid map, and fuse semantic labels into that grid map for semantic navigation on ROS.
insight: From the abstract only: mapping depth data to laser data lets a depth camera replace a laser scanner in standard 2D ROS navigation, and semantic labels on the grid map enable higher-level goals. No ablations are available to check this.
method: Dense point-cloud mapping: builds a dense point-cloud map using a deep convolutional neural network.
Depth-to-laser mapping: defines the mapping relationship between depth camera data and laser data so they can be interconverted.
Simulated-laser 2D grid map: builds a 2D raster (occupancy) map from laser data simulated from the depth camera.
Semantic fusion: integrates semantic information into the 2D grid map to enable semantic navigation of the service robot.

setting.backbone: deep convolutional neural network (unspecified) for dense mapping/semantics

results: The abstract only claims that the proposed system, compared with other robot navigation systems, better realizes interaction between service robots, people and the environment. No quantitative results are given.
limitations: Abstract only; no quantitative evaluation is reported.
Not evaluated on standard embodied navigation benchmarks.
